human_tolerance.notes: Breeds on Antarctic sea ice far from any settlement; the only human contact is research stations and tourism. Chicks in a creche grow more apprehensive after a helicopter approach to 1,000 m.

phases.name: breeding
phases.note: Courtship starts in March/April; the female lays a single egg in May or early June, incubated by the male for 65-75 days; chicks leave the colony in December/January.

phases.name: moult
phases.note: Yearly moult in January and February, taking around 34 days.

vocalizations.description: Courtship call of 1-2 seconds given during the ecstatic display: the male stands still, head on chest, then calls while moving around the colony. Pairs also duet face to face holding the posture for minutes.
Two-frequency-band calls used for individual recognition between mates, parents and offspring; chicks beg with a frequency-modulated whistle. The widest individual variation of any penguin.

conservation.note: Near Threatened (IUCN 3.1); Wikidata P141 with the downgrade history on Wikipedia.

range.note: Circumpolar in the Antarctic, almost exclusively between 66 and 77 degrees south; AQ is the ISO country for Antarctica.

traits.locomotion_modes.note: Flightless; walks with a wobbling gait or toboggans on land, swims at sea.

traits.flight.note: Like all penguins, flightless; wings stiffened into flippers.

traits.nest_type.note: Builds no nest; the single egg is balanced on the feet under a brood patch.

traits.mass_kg.note: Midpoint of Wikipedia's 22.7-45.4 kg range; mass varies strongly by sex and season (males fast ~120 days).

traits.length_m.note: Stonehouse (1975) average of 115 cm, via Wikipedia; adults 110-120 cm.

traits.lifespan_y.note: Average adult life expectancy 19.9 years at 95.1% yearly survival; 1% may reach 50.

traits.speed_ms.note: Midpoint of the 6-9 km/h average swimming speed (7.5 km/h = 2.08 m/s).

traits.diet.note: Fish usually the most important food (Antarctic silverfish the bulk), plus krill and squid. Shares are judgement; cephalopods counted under invertebrate because the schema has no mollusc key.

traits.social.note: Breeding colonies of up to several thousand individuals; ~595,000 adults across 46 colonies in 2009. Range is judgement.

traits.activity_pattern.note: 'Individuals may be active day or night.'

traits.defense.note: Adults are taken at sea by leopard seals and orcas; the response is flight (swimming away). No land predators of adults.

traits.wariness.note: Authored: little fear of people on foot (no land predators), but creche chicks grow apprehensive after helicopter approach.

habitat.use.note: Breeding cycle on the ice runs March-December with foraging trips to open water throughout; shares are judgement.

habitat.shelter_tag.note: Authored: the colony huddle on the ice is the shelter.

habitat.resources.note: Fish (silverfish, other Nototheniidae) mapped to small_vertebrate -- the tag vocabulary has no fish tag; krill and squid to invertebrate. Weights follow the diet shares.

habitat.human_tolerance.note: Avoider: breeds on remote sea ice; only research and tourism contact, with disturbance effects documented.

seasonal.strategy.note: Resident in the Antarctic year-round; disperses to the oceans January-March but does not migrate or go dormant.

seasonal.phases.note: Breeding and moult windows from Wikipedia; exact start/end days are judgement.

seasonal.life_stages.note: Chicks hatch July/August and leave December/January (~150 days), fledging at ~50% of adult weight.

vocalizations.ecstatic.note: Courtship in March/April; cooldown and loudness are judgement.

vocalizations.contact.note: Two-band individual-recognition calls; chick begging whistle. Cooldown and loudness are judgement.

look.note: Black head/back sharply delineated from white belly, pale-yellow breast, bright-yellow ear patches, 8 cm bill. Proportions authored for an upright flightless bird.

behavior.note: Authored bespoke program: no shared program models a colonial seabird that commutes over ice and dives. See species/aptenodytes-forsteri/behavior.json.
